Conventions These are the rules everything else follows. The design notes in .claude/internals/ give the reasons, and the source comments say more. State is Jotai, in one store. There are no context providers. Persisted settings are atomWithStorage atoms under keys starting with scmjs. , listed in Preferences ▸ Storage; each key must be registered in the reset table in src/atoms/preferencesAtoms.ts , and a test fails when one is not. The scenario is mutated in place. The parsed scenario that is written to disk is changed directly, not replaced, so React does not see an edit on its own. Each area has a revision counter, bumped after every edit, undo and load, that the viewport and panels subscribe to. The chrome shows some fields (map name, size, tileset) from a second set of atoms; change one side and you must change the other. Several maps can be open. The state atoms hold only the map in front; the others are parked records that a tab switch swaps in. A new piece of per-document state must be added to the park and install lists in src/atoms/documentAtoms.ts , or it leaks from one map into the next. Only changed sections are written. The scenario keeps the set of sections to re-encode on save, and everything else goes out byte for byte. Code that changes the scenario must mark every section it touched, or the change is silently lost on save. Edits are invertible change lists. A brush stroke, a placement or a paste produces a list of { before, after } changes per layer, applied in one fixed order and reversed for undo. A stroke is one history entry; the depth is a preference (Preferences ▸ Editing ▸ Undo, 200 by default). The settings dialogs and the trigger editors are OK / Apply / Cancel transactions, whose history entry is the difference between the tables before and after. Resize and the tileset change sit outside the undo model and clear it. Every write goes through the commits. The commit, undo and redo paths, the settings and trigger commits and the whole-document changes are where repainting, history and shared maps hook in. A new way of changing the scenario that bypasses them is invisible to the other people on a shared map. Dialogs are lazy. Adding one means an id in src/components/dialogs/ids.ts and an entry in the registry in DialogHost.tsx , which loads each dialog module on first use. Nothing on the startup path may import a dialog module statically, or Vite folds it back into the main chunk. Log what is worth explaining later. The editor keeps a log of what it did, which users read in View ▸ Debug Console and copy into bug reports. Log counts and labels, never payloads, and one line per user action, never per tile or per frame. Chatty lines go behind the console's Verbose tick. A render that throws is contained. Each dock panel, the palette, the map view and every dialog has an error boundary, with one last boundary around the whole application. A new top-level surface (a dock, a strip, a floating panel host) needs a boundary of its own. User-visible text goes through t() . See Translations . Plugins get the same API the editor uses. src/plugins/api.ts is the contract. A plugin's edit goes through the same transaction and history as a brush stroke. See The plugin host .

The plugin host plugins.md is written for someone who has the npm package and none of this repository. This is the editor's half: where the plugin system lives and how a plugin gets from an address to a running activate . File Holds src/plugins/api.ts The public types: the only place the contract is written src/plugins/host.ts Builds one plugin's API over the store; activation, deactivation, inspect and install src/plugins/loader.ts Spec parsing, the manifest fetch, and the fetch / transpile / import pipeline src/plugins/defaults.ts The plugins a fresh editor starts with, each pinned to a tag src/plugins/registry.ts Browse Plugins: reading, searching and caching the registry indexes src/plugins/widgets.ts api.ui.widgets : plain DOM in the editor's own class names, and the waiting kit src/plugins/claims.ts The trigger-list claims the trigger editors read src/plugins/images.ts Image loading, clipboard images, and drops and pastes in plugin dialogs src/plugins/failures.ts The toast a failed activation raises src/plugins/builtin.ts The vendored defaults in plugins/*/ , compiled in src/plugins/transpile.worker.ts TypeScript in a worker, for a .ts plugin loaded from source src/atoms/pluginAtoms.ts The installed list, stored code copies, runtimes, contributions, and the requests the viewport serves src/hooks/usePlugins.ts Activates the enabled plugins at startup and keeps the runtimes in step with the list src/components/dialogs/PluginDialogs.tsx Manage Plugins, Browse, the Add / Update confirmation, a plugin dialog's frame src/components/panels/PluginPanels.tsx The floating and docked frames a plugin's panel mounts into src/components/ui/DialogSlots.tsx The footer row a plugin's dialog slot mounts into The chrome reads the contributions: the menu bar merges plugin menu items into its model, the context menus and status bar add theirs, the right dock renders docked panels after Properties, and the hotkey hook checks plugin key combinations first. The viewport serves a plugin's map requests: picks, map tools and overlays. A plugin's document.edit commits one history entry through the same path a brush stroke takes, and document.update commits through the settings and trigger commits. document.sections rewrites the file and reloads it, which drops the history. While a map is shared, every one of those commits also reaches the session. plugins-host.md and sync.md in .claude/internals/ have the details. The loading pipeline # The spec is parsed into a base URL. builtin:<name> is a plugin compiled in from plugins/<name>/ ; a github: spec or a github.com URL resolves to raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/<ref or HEAD>/<dir>/ ; any other URL is a manifest, an entry file (a manifest is made up from its name) or a directory holding plugin.json . The manifest is fetched and validated; only name is required. The file to import is the manifest's build when it has one (a committed bundle, one fetch, no transpile), else its entry . That file is fetched as text and, if it is TypeScript, transpiled in the worker. Fetching as text matters: raw.githubusercontent.com serves text/plain , which a browser refuses to import as a module. Relative imports are followed depth first, and each file becomes a blob: module URL with its specifiers rewritten. An extensionless specifier is tried as .ts , .tsx , .mts , .js , .mjs and then as that directory's index.* ; ./x.js falls back to ./x.ts . Cycles and bare package names are errors naming the file. The module is imported and its default export (or a named activate ) is called with the API. Whatever it returns is kept for deactivation. Adding one # Pressing Add in Manage Plugins installs nothing. The editor canonicalises the address, asks GitHub which commit the ref points at, and reads the plugin.json at that commit. No code is fetched, transpiled or imported before the user agrees. The confirmation opens only once a manifest came back; an address with nothing behind it is reported under the Add field instead. The install has three ticks: Enable it now , Pin to this version (the stored spec becomes github:owner/repo@<sha> ) and Load from a copy saved here (below). The Update button on a pinned row previews the branch and, when it holds a different commit, reopens the same dialog with the old commit marked to be replaced. A listed plugin that is not running is still described: its manifest alone is fetched for the name, version, description and icon, and cached so the next visit shows them at once. Browse Plugins hands a chosen entry to the same Add path, so a registry decides what is listed and never what is trusted. Loading from a copy # Load from a copy saved here means "prefer the copy". With no copy yet, the load records every fetched file into browser storage (up to a size cap; a larger plugin stays remote with a console warning). With a copy, the load has no network path at all and fails on a file the copy lacks. Reload drops the copy and fetches again; turning the option off drops it too. Defaults and vendoring # The default plugins are ordinary plugins from their own repositories: Aftermath, Paint, Repair, scm-sim, scmjs.dev, scmscx.com, Stamp Library, Terrain from Image, TrigEdit, TrigScript and Walkability. All start on except TrigEdit, which is installed but off. Each is pinned in src/plugins/defaults.ts to a tag , never a branch, so a push to a plugin repository cannot change editors already in use, and any release can be rebuilt as it shipped. Moving a default forward is a commit that changes the tag there. A plugin's identity is its repository, whatever the version, so an older unpinned spec, the compiled-in copy and the pinned default are one plugin, not three. scripts/vendor-plugins.mjs writes each default's source at its tag into the gitignored plugins/ , where builtin.ts compiles it into the bundle. Every build does this, so a first visit loads no compiler and makes no third-party requests. The script runs from predev , prebuild and the desktop build, f

Tests Unit tests # Tests are tests/*.test.ts (and any src/**/*.test.ts ), run by vitest in Node with no browser. The whole suite takes a few seconds. The suites open two sets of map files: tests/maps/ is committed: five small .scx and .scm maps built by tests/support/testMaps.ts from the editor's own code, with nothing of Blizzard's in them. They cover the four file revisions, the three archive compressions, an archive without a file list, triggers, a briefing, locations, a sound and unit settings, but no terrain. tests/maps.test.ts fails when the files and the code that makes them disagree: run npm run test:maps and commit the result. Only generated maps go here. fixtures/maps/ holds Blizzard's own maps, on a machine that has them. The suites about terrain, doodads and what StarEdit itself writes need these, the extracted data in public/ , or both, and skip silently when the files are absent. CI has neither, so a green CI run has not exercised them. Run them locally before touching a tileset decoder, the doodad code, the isometric brush or anything under src/formats/ . Two suites are worth knowing about: tests/plugin-network.test.ts fetches, transpiles and imports the real default plugins from GitHub. It runs only with SCMJS_NETWORK_TESTS=1 ; CI runs it in the web build and the release pre-flight. tests/docs.test.ts checks these documents: the split into site pages, every relative link and picture, the 90-column wrap, and that the plugin guide names only calls the API declares. Browser tests # e2e/*.spec.ts are Playwright specs that drive the built editor in headless Chromium. They cover what the unit tests cannot: that the bundle starts, that each dialog's chunk loads and mounts, and that a change made through the chrome ends up in the saved file. npx playwright install chromium # once npm run build # the specs run against dist/ npm run test:e2e npx playwright test e2e/save.spec.ts # one file npx playwright test --ui # watch a spec run, step through it npm run test:e2e serves dist/ with vite preview on port 4173 and does not build, so build again after changing the editor. To run against something already being served, the dev server included, set SCMJS_E2E_URL to its address. Every spec runs under the same conditions, set up in e2e/support/editor.ts , so a run on a machine with game data is the run CI makes: No game data. Terrain is flat colours, and the editor offers Help ▸ Game Data… soon after it starts; a spec that uses the chrome closes that first. No network. Anything not served by the build under test is refused. No native file pickers. The editor opens through a file input and saves as a download, as in Firefox and Safari. A test also fails if the page threw or logged an error. Spec Checks boot.spec.ts A first visit: splash, editor, the Game Data offer, a blank map drawn dialogs.spec.ts Every dialog opens, in English and Korean save.spec.ts A map renamed and saved; every other section comes back byte for byte errors.spec.ts A dialog whose chunk fails closes with a notice; the editor carries on dataPage.spec.ts The Game Data page on its own installPage.spec.ts The page that installs game data for another page of the site moveIn.spec.ts Settings kept at the old address are brought over on the first visit pluginUpdates.spec.ts Checking all plugins for updates, and Update all docks.spec.ts Dragging a dock's edge over a plugin's map view rulers.spec.ts The rulers line up with the map past the scrollbars dialogs.spec.ts reads the dialog ids from the registry, so a new dialog is covered without touching the spec; one that renders nothing without a payload must be added to its NEEDS_PAYLOAD list. A failure leaves a trace under test-results/ ; npx playwright show-trace <trace.zip> replays it. CI runs the specs in the web build and keeps the report of a failed run.

Translations The editor's own words can be shown in another language; a map's text is never translated. English and Korean ship today, chosen in Preferences ▸ General or following the browser. Writing a string. The English text is the key: t("Save {name}", { name }) . The argument must be a string literal, since the extractor reads the source. A string kept in a table is marked msg("…") where it is written and shown with translate(value) . Never call t() at module scope, where the language is not yet known. Where one English word means two things, tc("menu", "Open") adds a context. Placeholders are a small subset of ICU MessageFormat: {name} , {n, plural, …} and {x, select, …} . Korean particles agree with the word before them through {name|을} . The catalogues. src/i18n/ko.json maps the English text to the Korean. After adding a string, run npm run i18n -- --write , which adds the new key with an empty value (shown in English until filled in) and drops keys nothing uses. tests/i18n.test.ts fails on a missing or unused key, a placeholder mismatch, or a t() whose argument is not a literal. Reviewing. npm run i18n -- --export ko ko.csv writes the catalogue as a spreadsheet with the source files each string appears in; --import ko ko.csv reads it back. The Korean was not written by a native speaker, and a native reader's review is welcome. Plugins get the same translator on api.i18n ; see plugins.md . .claude/internals/i18n.md covers adding a language and the Korean particle rules.

Desktop desktop/ is an Electron shell around the same web bundle. main.ts serves dist/ under app://scmjs/ , looks for a StarCraft installation and extracts the game data into the app's data folder, opens maps handed over by the file manager, guards the window's close while a map has unsaved changes, and holds the updater. preload.ts exposes that to the page as window.scmjsDesktop , typed in src/gamedata/desktop.ts . npm run desktop # bundle the main process and run Electron against dist/ SCMJS_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 npm run desktop # against the dev server instead npm run build:desktop # web build + main bundle + electron-builder for this OS npm run build:desktop takes the platform, architectures and targets on the command line; with none it builds this OS with the targets electron-builder.yml lists, which is what CI does: npm run build:desktop -- win # Windows: nsis + zip npm run build:desktop -- win nsis # just the installer npm run build:desktop -- linux AppImage x64 arm64 npm run build:desktop -- mac dmg arm64 npm run build:desktop -- --dir # unpacked app, no installer: the fast check npm run build:desktop -- win --skip-web # repackage the dist/ already on disk npm run build:desktop -- --skip-plugins # leave plugins/ alone (no vendoring fetch) Platforms are win , mac and linux ; architectures x64 , ia32 , arm64 , armv7l and universal ; any electron-builder target name ( nsis , dmg , zip , AppImage , deb , …) applies to every platform named. --skip-web and --skip-main reuse the bundles on disk; --publish <mode> and anything after a bare -- go to electron-builder unchanged. The script warns about cross-builds that need tooling the machine may lack (a macOS installer off a Mac, an NSIS installer without Wine) and runs them anyway; --dir and zip cross-build with nothing installed. Output lands in release/ . What ships. electron-builder.yml packs dist/ and desktop/dist/ only: never node_modules (Vite bundles everything) and never the game data a developer's public/ may hold. Windows gets an NSIS installer and a zip, macOS a dmg per architecture, Linux an AppImage and a .deb . The installers register .scm , .scx and .chk . Of Chromium's own UI locales only those of the editor's languages are included ( en-US and ko ): the editor's translations are in the bundle, but Chromium reports the system's language to the page only when its locale is there. A new language needs its locale added to electronLanguages . Builds are unsigned: Windows shows SmartScreen's "unrecognized app" screen, and macOS refuses the app until the user clears the quarantine attribute. What the build adds. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt in dist/ carries the licence of every runtime dependency and compiled-in plugin, generated from package.json . The desktop build and the container image also carry the runtimes the default plugins would otherwise download on first use (none of today's defaults declares one; eudplib's Pyodide and wheel, about 15 MB, did), so such a plugin needs no network there. scripts/bundle-plugin-runtimes.mjs reads a runtime.json from each pinned default's repository and puts the files in dist/plugin-runtime/<plugin>/<version>/ . The hosted editor and the web zip carry none. The app's data folder is %APPDATA%\scm-js on Windows, ~/.config/scm-js on Linux and ~/Library/Application Support/scm-js on macOS. It holds the extracted game data, the window geometry, and startup.log , the milestones of the last launch. SCMJS_TRACE=1 echoes them to the terminal. When a launch "hangs and then opens", that log tells a slow disk, a virus scanner and a slow first paint apart. From WSL , copy a Windows build to the Windows file system before running it. Started from \\wsl.localhost\… , a network share, it takes minutes to open. WSLENV passes the variable on to the Windows process: npm run build:desktop -- win --dir # release/win-unpacked cp -r release/win-unpacked /mnt/c/Users/<you>/scmjs-test SCMJS_TRACE=1 WSLENV=SCMJS_TRACE /mnt/c/Users/<you>/scmjs-test/scmJS.exe In-app updates # The desktop app checks GitHub releases at startup (a preference, on by default) and through Help ▸ Check for Updates…, using electron-updater over the latest*.yml files the release workflow uploads beside the installers. Finding one raises a toast with a Download button; nothing downloads or installs unasked, and installing goes through the same unsaved-changes check as closing the window. A nightly build follows the nightlies, a stable build follows stable releases, and a preference lets a stable install follow the nightlies. Windows, the AppImage and the .deb install updates themselves. macOS can see an update but not install it until the app is code-signed, so it offers the release page. A development run and an unpacked Linux folder report that they cannot check. desktop/updater.ts is the main-process side, src/editor/updates.ts the state machine, tests/updates.test.ts the cases.

Releases and hosting .github/workflows/build.yml has three channels: Channel Trigger What it produces ci every push to main and every pull request Lint, the unit and browser tests, and a web bundle that is thrown away nightly a daily cron at 07:17 UTC, or a manual run Installers, a web zip and the updater files on one rolling prerelease, and scmjs.dev/nightly stable a pushed vX.Y.Z tag A permanent release, the container image, scmjs.dev/editor and the docs site The nightly cron exits early when main has not moved since the last nightly. The nightly release is updated in place: its nightly tag is moved and its assets replaced, so there is one prerelease however many nights run. Its notes link scmjs.dev/nightly , which runs the same commit. Download links # GitHub redirects /releases/latest/download/<asset> to the newest release that is not a prerelease or a draft, so the download buttons on the site are plain links that never need updating and never resolve to a nightly: https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-windows-x64-setup.exe https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-windows-x64.zip https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-macos-arm64.dmg https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-macos-x64.dmg https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-linux-x86_64.AppImage https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-linux-amd64.deb https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/latest/download/scmJS-web.zip https://github.com/scm-js/scm-js/releases/download/nightly/scmJS-windows-x64-setup.exe The redirect can only resolve a fixed file name, so asset names carry no version; the version is in the release title, the notes and latest*.yml . To withdraw a bad release, tick "This is a pre-release" on it and the redirect falls back to the one before. The container image # docker/Dockerfile is nginx with the built web bundle and the default plugins' runtimes, pushed to ghcr.io/scm-js/scm-js on a tagged release only, as latest , the full version, and the moving X.Y and X . One manifest covers linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 . docker run --rm -p 8080:80 ghcr.io/scm-js/scm-js:latest # http://localhost:8080 npm run build:image # build it locally, tagged scmjs The image carries no game data: .dockerignore keeps the extracted trees out and docker/nginx.conf answers 404 for those paths, so a container asks through Help ▸ Game Data… like the hosted editor. Mounting an extracted tree is in game-data.md . Cutting a release # Run the Release workflow ( .github/workflows/release.yml ) from the Actions tab. It takes the version ( 0.3 , 1.0 and 1 are padded to three parts; blank releases the version the nightlies have been building), an optional notes box, and a dry_run tick that does everything except push. It refuses to run anywhere but main , refuses a version whose tag exists or that is not newer than the last release, and runs lint, the tests (the network suite included), the build and a check of the container image before writing anything. Then it commits the version into package.json and the lock file, tags that commit vX.Y.Z , and starts the Build workflow on the tag, which produces everything else. Nothing moves package.json on to a next version afterwards: on main it names the last release. A nightly is named <base>-nightly.<date>.<run number> , where the base is a patch bump of the newest release tag ( scripts/next-version.mjs ). Every job writes the version into package.json before building; Vite injects it as __APP_VERSION__ , read through src/version.ts , and electron-builder writes it into latest*.yml . The hand-written part of a release's notes comes from docs/releases/<version>.md (the full three-part name), committed to main before the release is cut, or from the Release workflow's notes input, which wins over the file. Either goes above GitHub's generated list of commits. The pre-flight prints what it found, so a dry run shows the body. docs/releases/README.md is the convention. The hosted builds # Address Deployed How scmjs.dev/editor on a tag, by the pages job GitHub Pages on this repository, built for /editor/ , served by the site's Cloudflare Worker scmjs.dev/nightly each nightly, by the nightly-site job The same commit built again for /nightly/ , pushed to scm-js/nightly , served by the same Worker docs.scmjs.dev on a tag, by the docs job, or by hand npm run build:docs , pushed to scm-js/docs The hosted editor is one release with everything else: the site, the installers, the image and the notes come from one tag. To put scmjs.dev/editor back on an older version, run Build on that tag. The docs site can also be deployed without a release, from Actions ▸ Docs site ▸ Run workflow, so a fix to the guides goes live at once; the next release replaces it with the tag's own pages. The nightly is built with SCMJS_SITE=nightly . The two editors share the scmjs.dev origin, because both need the game's page at /play/ beside them, and the nightly keeps its preferences, recent files and plugins under names of its own. The game data is the exception: both editors and the play page read one copy, so a nightly that changes how that copy is stored must keep it readable by the last release. Variables and secrets # None of these is required: a fork builds and releases without them, and a deploy that lacks its own is skipped with a notice. Name Kind For PAGES_BASE variable The hosted editor's base path ( /editor/ ); the repository name by default NIGHTLY_BASE variable The nightly's path on the site ( /nightly/ ); without it the nightly site is the web zip at a domain's root NIGHTLY_HOME variable The site the nightly is a path of; https://scmjs.dev by default NIGHTLY_DOMAIN variable The domain written into the nightly site's CNAME NIGHTLY_PAT secret A token with Contents: write on <owner>/nightly DOCS_DOMAIN , DOCS_PAT variable, secret The same pair for the docs site on <owner>/docs CI_BUILD_KEY

Docs site and screenshots docs.scmjs.dev is built by npm run build:docs . The guides are the eleven docs/*.md files, split at their ## headings into pages, with the ### beneath as each page's contents. The API reference is generated from the bundled plugin typings, so a doc comment in src/plugins/api.ts is a paragraph on the site. npm run build:docs # → docs-site/ (gitignored) python3 -m http.server 8000 -d docs-site # preview it at http://localhost:8000 node scripts/wrap-docs.mjs # rewrap the guides' prose at 90 columns node scripts/wrap-docs.mjs docs/guide.md # one file npm run docs:reference # the generated tables in triggers.md and chk-format.md The guides are read on GitHub as well. The site turns a relative link to one of the guides into a link to its page, and anything else in the repository into a link to GitHub. Prose is wrapped at 90 columns; tests/docs.test.ts fails on an unwrapped file, and scripts/wrap-docs.mjs fixes it, leaving code, tables, headings and generated blocks alone. The <!-- generated: … --> blocks in the trigger and CHK references are written from the code by npm run docs:reference ; never edit inside them. Guide screenshots # The pictures in the guides are docs/images/*.webp , made by scripts/guide-screenshots.mjs . It drives headless Chromium against the dev server, opens the fixture maps, sets up what each picture shows, and writes WebP files. Re-run it after a change to the chrome and commit the pictures that changed. npm run dev # in one terminal npm i --no-save playwright sharp # only this script needs them npx playwright install chromium # once node scripts/guide-screenshots.mjs # → docs/images/ node scripts/guide-screenshots.mjs --only units,fog node scripts/guide-screenshots.mjs --scenes plugin-guide It needs the game data and Big Game Hunters, Binary Burghs, Crescent Moon and Ground Zero from the game's Maps folder in fixtures/maps/ . Never commit a picture that shows anything but the editor. Some scenes have their own needs: plugin-guide needs no fixture map. Each picture is one of the examples in docs/plugins.md , run in the API Playground; changing an example that has a picture means re-running the scene. api-playground installs the API Playground plugin, which is not a default; --playground <url> points it at a local build. The scmjs.dev and shared-map pictures run against a stand-in for the service, scripts/lib/guide-scmjs-mock.mjs , which the script starts itself. When a dialog changes, change the scene; when a canned answer no longer fits, change the mock.

Contributing Keep the documents current. The eleven guides under docs/ are the documentation site and README.md is the repository's front page; a behaviour change that is not in them is undocumented. Write them for their readers, with src/ paths only in a guide's closing In the source section. Keep the matching note in .claude/internals/ in step too. Nothing of Blizzard's goes into git. Not the extracted data, not the archives, not the fixture maps. .gitignore covers the generated trees; check before adding a test fixture. Record where adapted code comes from. The rule is in ATTRIBUTION.md : a provenance comment beside adapted algorithms and tables, an entry there naming the source and licence, and the original notice kept. Run what CI runs : npm run lint , npm test and npm run build , and npm run test:e2e after a change to the chrome. With the game data and fixture maps on disk the real-data suites run too, and that is the run that counts for anything under src/formats/ . Plugin API changes are additive. PLUGIN_API_VERSION stays where it is for an addition. Document the addition in docs/plugins.md and with a doc comment in src/plugins/api.ts , which the reference is generated from. The example plugin at scm-js/plugin-hello-world should keep building. The plugins are separate repositories under github.com/scm-js . A change to the editor that a default plugin needs ships by moving that plugin's tag in src/plugins/defaults.ts .

API reference Everything a plugin can see and do, as the editor declares it. Plugin API version 1; generated from src/plugins/api.ts , the same declarations @scm-js/plugin-api publishes. A plugin is one activate(api) function. Everything below hangs off that argument. import type { PluginApi } from "@scm-js/plugin-api" ; export default function activate(api: PluginApi ) { api.menu.add( "Tools" , { label: "Say hello" , run: () => api.ui.toast({ title: "Hello" }) }); } Nothing here is written by hand. A member with no description has no doc comment in api.ts ; the fix belongs there, not on this page. An example marked Try it runs as it is written: the link opens it in the editor's API Playground , and nothing runs until you press Run. Groups api.document The open map: what it says, and the three ways of writing to it — edit (terrain and objects, one undo entry), update (the tables every dialog's OK writes) and sections (raw bytes). Opening, saving, exporting and closing are here too. api.settings The settings dialogs' tables, read-only; document.update writes them. api.triggers Reading triggers, and the pure helpers that make them presentable. Writing goes through document.update . api.terrain Reading the terrain: the tileset's paintable types, the ISOM lattice, flood regions, blend candidates and the symmetry mode. Painting goes through document.edit . api.tileset The loaded tileset graphics: whether they are there, and the decoded files behind them. api.selection What is selected on each object layer, the marked area, the active layer and the locked ones. api.clipboard Cut / Copy / Paste: the clip, its parts, and pasting — what the clipboard layer does. api.exchange The file formats behind File ▸ Import / Export: .trg and the strings text. api.palette The palettes' current picks — the terrain brush, the unit, sprite and doodad, the fog mode — and the placement options a plugin that places things should honour. api.names The names behind the numbers a map stores, so a plugin that shows raw values need not carry the game's tables itself. The per-map ones ( string , location , switch , player ) read the open scenario and answer a placeholder without one; the rest are the editor's own tables — the same names StarEdit shows. api.text StarCraft's <XX> text control codes: what they mean, and what a string looks like drawn. api.query Reading the open map: what is under a point, what lies in a rectangle, and the editor's own analyses — Check Map's issues, Tools ▸ Statistics, the Ctrl+F search and the string usage map the String Editor is built on. Everything here is a read: nothing changes the map, and nothing throws without one (an empty list, or null). api.data The game's own tables, as the editor decoded them: units.dat and its neighbours. names gives the labels, this gives the numbers — hit points, costs, build times, weapons, flags, the sprite and image each unit draws through. Everything is null until the tables are loaded ( load ), and stays null when the game data was never extracted. api.gameData Which set of game files the editor draws from — the game's own or a mod's — and installing, switching and removing sets. api.consts Bit masks, special unit ids and the pixels-per-tile every record is written in. api.graphics The pictures the viewport draws, for a plugin's own lists and previews: the same cached canvases, so asking for one costs nothing after the first time. Everything is null when the graphics it needs were never extracted — a plugin shows a name instead. api.view The map view: where the viewport is looking, how far in, and what it draws over the terrain. A plugin that finds something needs this to show the user where it is. api.ui Everything a plugin puts on the screen: the status line, toasts, dialogs, floating panels, confirm / alert / prompt / progress , a map tool that owns the pointer, a passive overlay drawn over the map, and picking an area or a tile. api.menu Items in the editor's menu bar. api.document DocumentApi The open map: what it says, and the three ways of writing to it — edit (terrain and objects, one undo entry), update (the tables every dialog's OK writes) and sections (raw bytes). Opening, saving, exporting and closing are here too. isOpen info scenario edit update undo redo history id list activate open create export save saveAs close renderImage test resize changeTileset extras sections buildSteps Members isOpen isOpen(): boolean ; info info(): DocumentInfo | null ; scenario scenario(): ReadonlyScenario | null ; The live scenario, for reading — see ReadonlyScenario . To change the map, use edit , update or sections . const scn = api.document.scenario(); if (scn) { const marines = scn.units.filter((u) => u.unitId === 0 ); api.ui.status( `${marines.length} marines on a ${scn.width} × ${scn.height} map` ); } Try it edit edit<R>(label: string , build: (tx: EditTransaction ) => Sync <R>): EditResult ; Run build against a transaction and record what it did as one undo entry. Operations apply as they are called, so later ones see earlier ones' results. Returns an all-zero result with changed: false when no map is open. build is synchronous — see Sync . Await what you need (graphics, a pick, a fetch) before the call, then write in one go. The transaction is closed when build returns; a call on it after that throws. A builder that throws is rolled back: what it had applied is taken off the map again, nothing reaches the history or the modified flag, and the error reaches you. // One undo entry called "Fill", however many operations it takes. await api.tileset.load(); // the async part first const [, ground] = api.terrain.types(); // the tileset's second flat terrain; none without the graphics const result = api.document.edit( "Fill" , (tx) => { if (ground) tx.stampTerrain({ x0: 0 , y0: 0 , x1: 8 , y1: 8 }, ground.id); tx.placeUnit(api.consts.unit.startLocation, 0 , 4 * api.consts.tile, 4 * api.consts.tile); }); api.ui.status( `${result.tiles} tiles, ${result.units} units` ); Try it update update<R>(label: string , build: (tx: UpdateTransaction ) => Sync <R>): UpdateResult ; The second kind of write: the tables and settings the dialogs edit — triggers, the string table, switch names, the scenario's own properties — as one transaction, the way a settings dialog's OK applies its whole form at once. Operations apply as they are called; the commit marks the map modified, bumps what the chrome reads and records what changed as one undo entry under label . build is synchronous, as edit 's is, and closed when it returns. An update is not rolled back, so a builder that throws leaves what it wrote: the sections it touched are committed — the map is modified, the chrome re-reads, the undo entry holds what was written — and the error reaches you. api.document.update( "Rename" , (tx) => { tx.properties({ name: "Lost Temple" , description: "Four players." }); }); Try it undo undo(): string | null ; redo redo(): string | null ; history history(): DocumentHistory ; The undo and redo stacks' tops — the labels the Edit menu shows — and their depths, without moving anything. const { undo } = api.document.history(); if (undo && ( await api.ui.confirm( `Undo "${undo}"?` ))) api.document.undo(); Try it id id(): number | null ; The id of the map in front — the one info() , scenario() and every write are about — or null with no map. Stable for the map's life, so a plugin can key what it keeps per map on it. (Null too for a scenario a test put in place without the editor.) list list(): OpenDocumentInfo []; Every open map, in the order the editor lists them, the one in front marked active . Empty with no map. The list changes only through open , create , activate and close (by any plugin or the user), each of which fires the "document" event. for ( const map of api.document.list()) api.log(map.id, map.name, map.active ? "(in front)" : "" ); Try it activate activate(id: number ): boolean ; Bring an open map to the front, as clicking its tab does: its history, selections and view come back as they were left, and the "document" event fires with reason "switch" . Nothing is re-read. True once it is in front (at once, when it already was); false for an id that is not open. isPreserved isPreserved(trigger: ReadonlyTrigger ): boolean ; setPreserved setPreserved(trigger: ReadonlyTrigger , on: boolean ): TriggerRecord ; triggersFor triggersFor(list: readonly ReadonlyTrigger [], groups: readonly number []): number []; The indices of the triggers any of these player groups own. summarize summarize(trigger: ReadonlyTrigger , briefing?: boolean ): { players: string ; conditions: string ; actions: string ; }; The three lines the trigger list shows: players, conditions, actions. for ( const trigger of api.triggers.list()) { const line = api.triggers.summarize(trigger); api.log( `${line.players}: ${line.conditions} → ${line.actions}` ); } Try it comment comment(trigger: ReadonlyTrigger ): string | null ; A trigger's Comment action text, when it has one. epd epd(address: number ): number ; EUD: the player value that reaches a memory address through the deaths table ( (address − consts.triggers.deathsTable) / 4 , the address rounded down to a dword) — what a Deaths condition or Set Deaths action stores in player with unitId 0 to read or write that dword. addressOf addressOf(player: number , unitId?: number ): number ; EUD: the address a record's player and unitId reach through the deaths table — epd 's inverse, and a plain death counter's cell as an address. fingerprint fingerprint(trigger: ReadonlyTrigger ): string ; A content fingerprint of a trigger: the same wherever it sits in the list and whatever the game's bookkeeping bits say. What a plugin that generates triggers finds its run by ( TriggerClaimSpec.locate ), and what an editor keeps a selection by across a list that changed under it. usage usage(list?: readonly ReadonlyTrigger []): { cells: [ player: number , unit: number ][]; switches: number []; }; Every death-counter cell ( [player, unit] ) and switch the triggers read or write — TRIG when list is omitted. A player group counts as every slot it can resolve to ( Current Player as the trigger's owners); a class unit ( Any unit , Men , …) counts for nothing, and an EUD player is an address, not a cell. What a plugin that allocates counters or switches of its own must keep clear of. // A switch no trigger touches, for a plugin that needs one of its own. const taken = new Set(api.triggers.usage().switches); const free = Array . from ({ length: 256 }, (_, i) => i).find((i) => !taken.has(i)); api.log(free === undefined ? "every switch is in use" : `${api.names.switch(free)} is free` ); Try it references references(list?: readonly ReadonlyTrigger [], options?: { briefing?: boolean ; }): TriggerRefs []; What each trigger reads, writes and names — TRIG when list is omitted, one entry per trigger in list order. A condition reads (a switch, a death counter, the timer, a player's ore, units at a location); an action writes (Set Switch, Set Deaths, Create Unit, Move Location's target, Victory) or uses something without changing it (the location units appear at, the text a message shows, a sound). Player groups are resolved to slots against the map's forces, Current Player as the trigger's owners; a Deaths record past the counters is a memory reference with its address. What a plugin needs to draw how triggers depend on each other, find a switch that is set and never tested, or answer "which triggers can end the game". With briefing , MBRF, where only strings and sounds are referred to. // Switches something tests that nothing ever sets. const refs = api.triggers.references().flatMap((t) => t.refs).filter((r) => r.kind === "switch" ); const set = new Set(refs.filter((r) => r.access === "write" ).map((r) => r.id)); const never = [... new Set(refs.filter((r) => r.access === "read" && !set.has(r.id)).map((r) => r.id))]; Try it resolvePlayers resolvePlayers(group: number , owners?: readonly number []): { players: readonly number []; approximate: boolean ; }; The 0-based player slots a player group names on the open map: a slot itself, the members of a force, players 1–12 for All Players (as conditions and the unit actions take it; as a trigger's owner it is players 1–8), and for Current Player the slots of owners (the groups a trigger is ticked for). approximate when the group is only settled while the game runs ( Foes , Allies , Neutral Players , Non Allied Victory Players ); players is then every slot it could name. claim claim(spec: TriggerClaimSpec ): TriggerClaimHandle ; Tell the editor that a run of the trigger list is generated by this plugin. The Trigger Editor badges those rows, locks them and offers the plugin's own editor in place of the form; the Text Trigger Editor fences them in comments; Import Triggers says what a replace would remove. The claim lives until remove() or the plugin's deactivation; call refresh() after a rebuild so the editors ask locate again. // Fingerprints of the triggers thi

api.text TextApi StarCraft's <XX> text control codes: what they mean, and what a string looks like drawn. Bytes 0x01–0x1F in a string are colour and layout codes. This is the editor's own table of what each one does — the same one the String Editor's buttons and preview are drawn from — plus the reading of a string that turns those bytes into what the game shows. A plugin that displays or rewrites map text should use this rather than carrying a copy: the numbering is easy to get wrong (the editor's own table was, from 0x12 up, until it was checked against the classic player palette). Remastered runs models Remastered's rule, where a colour set on one line carries onto the next. StarCraft 1.16.1 reset the colour at every line break, so a string written before the remaster can draw in colours its author never chose — bleedingLines finds exactly those lines and fixBleeding writes the reset the old game supplied. Pass resetPerLine to runs to see the old rendering. The other thing the old game did and a modern renderer does not is honour every alignment code on a line, stacking the pieces between them in one place: stackedLines finds those lines and flattenStacks lays them out left to right. runs is one of the renderers that cannot show them — TextLine.align is one alignment for the whole line. codes code insertable defaultColor runs plain escape bleedingLines fixBleeding stackedLines flattenStacks Members codes codes(): TextCode []; Every byte the game gives a meaning, in order; rgb is set for the colours only. code code(byte: number ): TextCode | null ; One byte's meaning, or null for a byte the game ignores. insertable insertable(): TextCode []; The codes worth offering as buttons: no tab, newlines or the do-nothing byte. defaultColor defaultColor(): string ; #rrggbb — what the game starts a string in, and what 1.16.1 reset to at a line break. runs runs(text: string , options?: RunOptions ): TextLine []; The string split into lines of coloured runs, the way the game draws it. plain plain(text: string ): string ; The text with every control byte removed — what the string actually says. escape escape(byte: number ): string ; <0E> , the way every StarCraft editor writes a control byte. bleedingLines bleedingLines(text: string ): BleedingLine []; The lines of text that Remastered draws in a colour 1.16.1 did not: a line that sets no colour of its own, after one that left a colour set. Empty for a single-line string. fixBleeding fixBleeding(text: string ): string ; text with the default colour written at the head of every bleeding line, so both games draw it alike. Idempotent, and never changes what the string says. stackedLines stackedLines(text: string ): StackedLine []; The lines of text that 1.16.1 drew at more than one alignment at once — the "stacked" lobby and unit names a classic map is built with. A line whose only alignment code sits at its head is not one: that code places the line. flattenStacks flattenStacks(text: string ): string ; text with every stacked line laid out left to right: the alignment codes that split it dropped and its pieces joined in writing order, a space between two that would otherwise run together. Colours and every other byte survive, so nothing the string says is lost — only where each piece sat. Idempotent. Types Declarations only this group names. CodeEffect type type CodeEffect = "color" | "mimic" | "invisible" | "align" | "clip" | "nothing" | "space" ; What a control byte does. Colours carry an rgb ; the rest are layout or visibility. TextCode interface interface TextCode byte: number code: string <0E> , the way every StarCraft editor writes it. label: string effect: CodeEffect rgb: string | null #rrggbb for effect: "color" , else null. player?: number Which player's colour this is, for the ones that are a player colour (1-based). Align type type Align = "left" | "right" | "center" ; TextRun interface interface TextRun One stretch of text in a single colour. text: string color: string #rrggbb ; the default colour until a code says otherwise. invisible: boolean After <0B> / <14> : the game draws nothing, but the text is still there. clipped: boolean After <0C> in the large font: the rest of the line is dropped. TextLine interface interface TextLine runs: TextRun [] align: Align RunOptions interface interface RunOptions resetPerLine?: boolean Reset to DEFAULT_TEXT_COLOR at every newline, the way 1.16.1 did. Remastered carries the colour across, which is the default here. initialColor?: string What <01> mimics and what the string starts in. BleedingLine interface interface BleedingLine line: number 0-based index of the line that inherits a colour it did not set. carried: TextCode The code Remastered carries onto it — the whole entry, so a caller can name it. StackedLine interface interface StackedLine A line the game draws in more than one place at once. 0x12 and 0x13 move the text that follows them to the right or the centre of the line they are on, and 1.16.1 honoured every one of them: Name<12>by Author drew Name at the left and by Author at the right of the same line. Lobby names, unit names and briefings were built out of that — the "stacked" text a classic map shows and a renderer that takes one alignment for the whole line does not. runsOf is one of those renderers: TextLine.align holds a single alignment, the last one the line set, so every piece before it lands somewhere its author did not choose. line: number 0-based index of the line within the string. pieces: number How many pieces of text the line draws, each at its own alignment. api.gameData GameDataApi Which set of game files the editor draws from — the game's own or a mod's — and installing, switching and removing sets. The game data as a whole: which set of files the editor draws from, and installing, switching and removing sets — the plugin side of Help ▸ Game Data…. What is in the files is data (the tables), tileset (the graphics), graphics (the pictures) and names (the labels, which follow the loaded set: a unit, weapon, upgrade or technology a mod renamed shows its new name, and the rest keep StarEdit's). A data set is a name over files in the game's own formats; a mod that extends the tables past the game's sizes is not covered. Installing needs the game's two archives every time, since a mod's files are laid over them the way its loader lays them. source profile profiles install select remove read Members source source(): GameDataSource | null ; The session's source, or null while it is still being resolved at startup. profile profile(): GameDataProfile ; The data set in use — the game's own until another is selected. profiles profiles(): Promise < GameDataProfile []>; Every data set with a copy here, the game's own first. install install(profile: GameDataProfile , files: GameDataFiles , progress?: (fraction: number , label: string ) => void ): Promise < GameDataSource >; Extract a data set from its files, store it under profile.id and switch to it. The archives must include the game's own two; the promise rejects with the reason when they do not or the extraction fails. progress is 0–1 with a label, as the dialog's bar. select select(id: string ): Promise < GameDataSource >; Switch to a data set. Everything decoded from the previous one is dropped and the viewport redraws from the new files; a set with no copy here falls back to the game's own. Resolves with the source in use afterwards. remove remove(id: string ): Promise < boolean >; Remove a data set's copy (never the game's bundled files). True when there was one. read read(path: string ): Promise <Uint8Array | null >; One file of the data set in use, by its path in the extracted copy: the archive path in lower case with forward slashes ( arr/units.dat , tileset/jungle.cv5 , unit/zerg/drone.grp ). tileset/manifest.json and unit/manifest.json list what was extracted. Null when the copy has no such file, or there is no game data. Types Declarations only this group names. GameDataProfile interface interface GameDataProfile A data set: one set of game files the editor draws from. The default is the game's own; any other is a mod's, installed under an id of its own, the same formats and table sizes with some of the files replaced. id: string Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, up to 40 characters. name: string What the dialog and the status line call it. GameDataSource interface interface GameDataSource Where the session's game data comes from. kind: "bundled" | "stored" | "none" bundled (this build's own files, or the desktop app's extraction), stored (a copy kept in the browser), or none . label: string One line, as Help ▸ Game Data… shows it. profile: GameDataProfile The data set the files belong to. desktop: boolean Set when the desktop app extracted the files from a StarCraft installation. GameDataBytes type type GameDataBytes = Blob | Uint8Array; Bytes for an install: a File / Blob , or already an array. GameDataFiles interface interface GameDataFiles What a data set is installed from. archives: readonly { name: string ; data: GameDataBytes ; }[] The archives, StarDat.mpq and BrooDat.mpq among them — a mod replaces files, it does not bring the rest. The game's own are read first, then the others in the order given, later ones winning as in the game. files?: readonly { path: string ; data: GameDataBytes ; }[] Loose files by member path ( arr/units.dat , unit/terran/marine.grp ), read before any archive.

api.consts ConstsApi Bit masks, special unit ids and the pixels-per-tile every record is written in. The constants a plugin needs to write a record rather than read one: the bit masks in a UNIT / THG2 / MRGN record, the condition, action and argument numbers of a TRIG / MBRF one, the few unit ids the game itself treats specially, and the one conversion — 32 pixels to a tile — every object position goes through. They are the editor's own ( sections/objects.ts , editor/units.ts ) and they arrive here at run time rather than in the typings on purpose: @scm-js/plugin-api is erased before the loader ever sees the specifier, so a value imported from that package type-checks and is then undefined. Anything a plugin needs while it runs has to come off api . Without this a plugin writes the hex itself, which is how a sprite's kind came to be read as flags & 0x1000 in three places. tile unit sprite location triggers isResource Members tile readonly tile: 32 ; Map pixels to a tile. UNIT and THG2 store pixels; MTXM, MRGN and the brushes count tiles. unit readonly unit: UnitConsts ; UNIT: the special unit ids, the default resource amounts, and the record's four bit masks. sprite readonly sprite: SpriteConsts ; THG2: the sprite record's flag word. location readonly location: LocationConsts ; MRGN: the Anywhere slot, and the elevation bits. triggers readonly triggers: TriggerConsts ; TRIG / MBRF: the condition and action types, and the enumerated arguments. isResource isResource(unitId: number ): boolean ; Whether a unit type is a mineral field or a vespene geyser. api.graphics GraphicsApi The pictures the viewport draws, for a plugin's own lists and previews: the same cached canvases, so asking for one costs nothing after the first time. Everything is null when the graphics it needs were never extracted — a plugin shows a name instead. ready load unitImage spriteImage tileImage doodadImage renderRect renderClip playerColor requestUnit requestSprite icon requestIcons onImageLoaded Members ready ready(): { tileset: boolean ; units: boolean ; }; Whether the tileset graphics and the unit tables are in memory. load load(): Promise <{ tileset: boolean ; units: boolean ; }>; Fetch both; resolves with what is available afterwards. unitImage unitImage(unitId: number , options?: { owner?: number ; }): PluginImage | null ; A unit type in its editor pose, in a player's colours ( owner 0 by default). spriteImage spriteImage(kind: SpriteKind , id: number , options?: { owner?: number ; flipped?: boolean ; }): PluginImage | null ; A THG2 sprite: a sprites.dat image for "pure" , a unit for "unit" . tileImage tileImage(tileId: number ): PluginImage | null ; One 32 × 32 megatile of the open map's tileset. doodadImage doodadImage(doodadId: number ): PluginImage | null ; A doodad drawn from its own tiles. renderRect renderRect(rect: Rect , options?: Partial < MapImageOptions >): Promise <Blob | null >; Part of the map as File ▸ Export ▸ Image draws it — the same render, cropped to a tile rect. Everything it needs is loaded first; null without a map or a canvas. renderClip renderClip(clip: Clip , options?: RenderClipOptions ): PluginImage | null ; A Clip drawn as the clipboard layer's paste ghost draws it: the picture (its own tiles, or the catalogue's for a doodad-only clip), then units, sprites and doodad overlays with the viewport's own graphics, then location boxes — a thumbnail for a list of clips, or the ghost under the pointer while a plugin stamps one. It is drawn with the graphics of the clip's own tileset ( clip.era ), which are in memory for the open map once loaded; a clip from another tileset answers null until tileset.load(id) has fetched that one. So does a missing tileset or a page with no canvas. Synchronous and uncached: keep the result while the clip and the tileset stay the same. playerColor playerColor(owner: number ): string ; The colour a player's units are drawn in, #rrggbb . requestUnit requestUnit(unitId: number ): boolean ; Start fetching the GRPs a unit type needs, and say whether they are already in memory. Graphics load lazily, so the first unitImage for a type is often null — ask for it here, redraw on onImageLoaded , and the list fills in. requestSprite requestSprite(kind: SpriteKind , id: number ): boolean ; icon icon(kind: IconKind , id: number , options?: { look?: IconLook ; }): PluginImage | null ; The game's own button picture for a unit type, an upgrade or a technology — the icon its command card shows — 36 × 34 at most and transparent round the edges. look colours it as the game does: "normal" yellow (the default), "disabled" grey, "selected" white. It does not depend on the map or its tileset. Null for an id with no picture (a unit type past 227, a turret) and until requestIcons has the pictures; null for good from a game data copy made before the editor kept them (installing the game data again brings them). The canvas is the editor's own cached one: draw from it. // A row of what a player researched, as the game's icons, with the names where there are no pictures. const show = () => list.replaceChildren(...done.map((r) => { const icon = api.graphics.icon(r.kind, r.id); if (!icon) return api.ui.el( "span" , {}, r.kind === "tech" ? api.names.tech(r.id) : api.names.upgrade(r.id)); const canvas = api.ui.el( "canvas" , { width: icon.width, height: icon.height }); canvas.getContext( "2d" )?.drawImage(icon.image, 0 , 0 ); return canvas; })); api.graphics.requestIcons(); api.graphics.onImageLoaded(show); show(); requestIcons requestIcons(): boolean ; Start fetching the icon pictures (one sheet holds them all), and say whether they are in memory. onImageLoaded fires when they arrive. onImageLoaded onImageLoaded(listener: () => void ): Disposable ; A GRP finished loading: anything drawn from one may look different now. Types Declarations only this group names. IconKind type type IconKind = "unit" | "upgrade" | "tech" ; IconLook type type IconLook = "normal" | "disabled" | "selected" ; PluginImage interface interface PluginImage A picture the editor already has: the canvas it draws from, and its size in pixels. image: HTMLCanvasElement width: number height: number RenderClipOptions interface interface RenderClipOptions pixelsPerTile?: number Pixels per tile; 32 (the game's own) by default. A thumbnail wants 4–8. parts?: Partial < ClipParts > Which parts to draw; every part the clip carries by default. Seen in Stamp Library clips kept in storage, drawn as thumbnails and pasted as one edit Timelapse following every commit, one frame per change Aftermath replays opened as view-only maps, with the game shown in the map's place

api.view ViewApi The map view: where the viewport is looking, how far in, and what it draws over the terrain. A plugin that finds something needs this to show the user where it is. zoom setZoom visible center reveal goTo cursorTile flags setFlags gridSize setGridSize flash Members zoom zoom(): number ; setZoom setZoom(zoom: number ): void ; 0.25 … 8, as the zoom control's steps. visible visible(): Rect ; The tiles on screen. center center(x: number , y: number ): void ; Scroll so a tile is in the middle of the viewport. reveal reveal(rect: Rect , options?: RevealOptions ): Promise < boolean >; Bring a tile rect onto the screen, gliding there by the shortest way rather than jumping, and leaving the view alone when the rect is already visible. With fit the view zooms out (never in) as far as the rect needs. Resolves once the view is there; false when the user, or another request, moved it first — a plugin that follows its own work around the map takes that as its cue to stop. const shown = await api.view.reveal({ x0: 0 , y0: 0 , x1: 16 , y1: 16 }, { fit: true }); if (!shown) api.log( "the user moved the view first" ); Try it goTo goTo(target: GoTo ): void ; Scroll to an object (and select it, for a unit, sprite or location). // Player 1's start location, selected and in the middle of the view. const start = api.query.startLocations().find((s) => s.owner === 0 ); if (start) api.view.goTo({ kind: "unit" , index: start.index }); Try it cursorTile cursorTile(): { x: number ; y: number ; }; The tile under the pointer, as the status bar shows it. flags flags(): ViewFlags ; The View menu's ticks: grid, locations, units, sprites, doodads, fog, … setFlags setFlags(patch: Partial < ViewFlags >): void ; api.view.setFlags({ grid: !api.view.flags().grid }); Try it gridSize gridSize(): number ; Grid spacing in map pixels (32 = one tile). setGridSize setGridSize(size: 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 ): void ; flash flash(target: FlashTarget ): void ; Highlight something on the map for a moment: the rect an edit filled, the units it placed, the location it moved. Fades by itself; several may run at once. Nothing to clean up. // Mark the top-left corner for Player 1's fog, and show where that was. const rect = { x0: 0 , y0: 0 , x1: 8 , y1: 8 }; const r = api.document.edit( "Fog a corner" , (tx) => tx.setFog(rect, 0b1 , "fog" )); if (r.changed) api.view.flash({ rect }); Try it Types Declarations only this group names. ViewFlags interface interface ViewFlags grid: boolean locations: boolean locationNames: boolean units: boolean sprites: boolean doodads: boolean Off draws the ground under the doodads (TILE) instead of the picture (MTXM). fog: boolean elevation: boolean Ground height per minitile, tinted (mid amber, high red). buildability: boolean Unbuildable tile groups, hatched in blue. startLocations: boolean animateWater: boolean Cycle the palette so water and lava animate as they do in game. animateUnits: boolean Run the units' iscript idle animations (turrets, pulsing buildings, fires, smoke). hdGraphics: boolean Draw terrain and sprites from StarCraft: Remastered's 2x pictures, where the data set in use has them. GoTo type type GoTo = { kind: "tile" ; x: number ; y: number ; } | { kind: "unit" ; index: number ; } | { kind: "sprite" ; index: number ; } | { kind: "location" ; index: number ; } /** Opens the Trigger Editor (or, with `briefing`, the Mission Briefing) on that trigger. */ | { kind: "trigger" ; index: number ; briefing?: boolean ; }; Where view.goTo should take the user. Issues from query.validate carry one. RevealOptions interface interface RevealOptions How view.reveal brings a rect on screen. fit?: boolean Zoom out to the zoom control's nearest step that fits the rect (plus the margin); never zooms in. Off by default. animate?: boolean Glide rather than jump. On by default. margin?: number Tiles kept clear between the rect and the viewport's edge when the view has to move. 1 by default. FlashTarget type type FlashTarget = { rect: Rect ; kind?: FlashKind ; ms?: number ; } | { units: number []; kind?: FlashKind ; ms?: number ; } | { locations: number []; kind?: FlashKind ; ms?: number ; } | { tiles: { x: number ; y: number ; }[]; kind?: FlashKind ; ms?: number ; }; What view.flash highlights: a tile rect, or units / locations by index. The highlight fades over ms (600 by default) and never blocks or takes the pointer; it is the shared way to say "this just changed" or "look here", so every plugin's flash looks the same. kind picks the colour: "change" (gold, the default) or "attention" (teal). FlashKind type type FlashKind = "change" | "attention" ; Seen in Walkability a read-only overlay drawn over the map Trigger Map the trigger list as a graph, from what each trigger reads and writes

api.ui UiApi Everything a plugin puts on the screen: the status line, toasts, dialogs, floating panels, confirm / alert / prompt / progress , a map tool that owns the pointer, a passive overlay drawn over the map, and picking an area or a tile. openDialogs status statusText toast saveFile dialog panel fileType mapView statusItem mapButton dialogSlot preferencesPage mapTool overlay pickFiles pickArea pickTile pickObject loadImage readClipboardImage confirm alert prompt progress tooltip el widgets open ask repaint Members openDialogs openDialogs(): string []; The dialogs open now, bottom to top, by id: the built-in ones by their DialogId , a plugin's as "pluginDialog" . What a shared map shows others ("in Player Settings"). status status(text: string ): void ; Set the status bar line. statusText statusText(): string ; The status bar line as it stands. toast toast(toast: { kind?: Toast [ "kind" ]; title: string ; detail?: string ; ttl?: number ; }): void ; A short notice over the map that leaves by itself — how Save reports; ttl 0 keeps it until dismissed. api.ui.toast({ kind: "ok" , title: "Export finished" , detail: "12 triggers written." }); Try it saveFile saveFile(data: Blob | Uint8Array, fileName: string ): Promise <{ route: "picker" | "download" ; fileName: string ; } | null >; Write a file to disk the way the editor's own exports do: into the file the browser's save dialog picks, or as a download where there is no dialog. Resolves with where it went, or null when the user dismissed the dialog. dialog dialog(spec: DialogSpec ): DialogHandle ; panel panel(spec: PanelSpec ): PanelHandle ; Open a panel: floating over the map, docked at the right with the built-in panels, or in the strip under the map ( spec.dock ). As many as you like; each closes with the plugin. fileType fileType(spec: FileTypeSpec ): Disposable ; Claim a kind of file: dropped on the editor or picked in File ▸ Open, a file with one of spec.extensions is handed to spec.open instead of being opened as a map. A plugin that claims what another already has is not given it (the first stays); none can claim the editor's own .scm , .scx or .chk . Ends with the plugin, or with dispose . api.ui.fileType({ name: "StarCraft replay" , extensions: [ ".rep" ], open: (files) => loadReplays(files) }); mapView mapView(spec: MapViewSpec ): MapViewHandle ; Another way to look at the maps you choose, in the map's place, with a switch over the map between it and the map itself (see MapViewSpec ). A map shows one view at a time; each map keeps the one it was left on. Ends with the plugin, or with dispose . const game = api.ui.mapView({ title: "Game" , mount: (el) => { el.append(frame); } }); // A map just opened is the one in front. if ( await api.document.open(map, "replay.scx" , { viewOnly: { label: "Replay" } })) game.show( true ); statusItem statusItem(spec: StatusItemSpec ): StatusItemHandle ; A cell of your own in the status bar. One line of text beside the plugin's icon, a spinner while busy , a click. Keep the handle and set it as things move; it leaves with remove() or the plugin. mapButton mapButton(spec: MapButtonSpec ): MapButtonHandle ; A button on the map, in the row at its bottom-right corner beside the tileset, size and zoom — for something that belongs to the map being worked on, such as a shared map's chat. Keep it to what matters while the map is in view; everything else goes in a menu or the status bar. It leaves with remove() or the plugin. dialogSlot dialogSlot(dialog: DialogSlotId , spec: DialogSlotSpec ): Disposable ; Add to a built-in dialog. mount runs in a row at the left of the dialog's footer each time that dialog opens, with the dialog's working-copy fields to read and fill ( SlottedDialogId lists which dialogs and fields) — or to another plugin's dialog, by the id its DialogSpec.slot offers. Returns the registration; it leaves with dispose() or the plugin. // A button in Map Properties that tidies the name in the form. The user still presses OK. api.ui.dialogSlot( "mapProperties" , { mount(body, dlg) { body.append(api.ui.widgets.button( "Tidy name" , { onClick: () => { dlg.fields.name.set(dlg.fields.name.get().trim().replace(/\s+/g, " " )); } })); }, }); Try it preferencesPage preferencesPage(spec: PreferencesPageSpec ): Disposable ; A page of the plugin's own in Edit ▸ Preferences, under Plugins — see PreferencesPageSpec . ui.open("preferences", { page: "plugin:<id>" }) opens it. Returns the registration; it leaves with dispose() or the plugin. mapTool mapTool(spec: MapToolSpec ): MapToolHandle ; Take over the pointer on the map until stop() , Esc, a right-click, a map change or another tool. One tool runs at a time — starting one stops the previous — and a pickArea / pickTile in progress is served first. overlay overlay(spec: OverlaySpec ): OverlayHandle ; A picture over the map the user can switch on and off (a tick in the View menu, the Layers panel) and that stays while they work on any layer. It draws at every repaint and hears the pointer, but never takes it. As many as you like; they go with the plugin. pickFiles pickFiles(options?: PickFilesOptions ): Promise <File[]>; The browser's file picker; resolves with an empty list on cancel. pickArea pickArea(options?: PickOptions ): Promise < Rect | null >; Let the user drag a rectangle on the map. The viewport switches to a crosshair, draws the marquee and takes the gesture ahead of the active layer's tools; resolves with the tile rect (exclusive x1 / y1 ), or null when the user pressed Esc or right-clicked, no map is open, the map was replaced, or the plugin was disabled. Only one pick runs at a time — a new one cancels the previous. A modal dialog covers the map, so close yours first and reopen it with the result. pickTile pickTile(options?: PickOptions ): Promise <{ x: number ; y: number ; } | null >; As pickArea , for a single click: the tile under it. pickObject pickObject(options?: PickObjectOptions ): Promise < PickedObject | null >; As pickTile , fo

""}` ) }); // `after` puts an item directly under a built-in one, named by its English label. api.menu.add( "File" , { label: "Open from My Site…" , after: "Open Recent" , run: () => api.ui.status( "…" ) }); Try it Types Declarations only this group names. TopMenu type type TopMenu = "File" | "Edit" | "View" | "Layer" | "Scenario" | "Triggers" | "Tools" | "Plugins" | "Help" ; MenuPath type type MenuPath = TopMenu | `${TopMenu}/${string}` | ( string & {}); A top-level menu, or a submenu by label: "File/Import" . Give this or command . command?: string A registered command's id, instead of a run of its own.
